written: 2026-11-20, after SeedLM-9, before the cross-coder ensemble ran on any evaluation set
motivation: Agreement inside one coder's beam picked worse programs than the beam's first (SeedLM-7): the beam's wrong programs are variants of one mistake. The consensus round found agreement useful between sources that fail differently. Seven post-coders now exist that differ in data mix and run (s4-post, s5-var, s6-graft, s6-comp, s8-all, s9-early, s9-early-last); two runs of the same mix differed by 9 on held-out teacher tasks, so their mistakes are at least partly independent
hypothesis: Among the first verified programs of separately trained coders, the behaviour on probe inputs that the most coders share is correct more often than any single coder's program
method: scripts/seedlm10_ensemble.py, coders in the order s5-var, s8-all, s6-graft, s6-comp, s9-early, s9-early-last, s4-post: each coder's first verified program at beam width 32; 24 probe inputs from the consensus probe grammar; two proposals agree when at least 3 probes give both a value and none differ; the proposal with the most agreeing coders (itself included) wins, ties to the earliest in the order. Nothing here is tuned on any evaluation set
primary_measure: held-out teacher tasks (139): the vote's program is correct on all three cases. Supported if the vote solves at least 3 more than the best single coder in the ensemble; not supported if it solves fewer than the best single coder; inconclusive otherwise
secondary_measures: held-out development fifth (94): the vote alone against each coder alone, and the engine-backed method (the engine's program unless the engine marks it not confident, then the vote's) against the same rule with s5-var's first verified program
choice: if the engine-backed vote solves more of the held-out development fifth than 69 (s5-var's best method), it becomes a candidate method and gets the validation gate (alone no fewer than the engine's 19 of 45; in the 1.5B pipeline no fewer than 31), one MBPP+ test run and one HumanEval+ run

outcome.primary: held-out teacher tasks: the vote solves 70 of 139; the best single coder (s8-all) 62, s5-var 52, the others 51 to 61; some coder's proposal is correct for 90. +8 over the best single coder: supported (reports/seedlm/ensemble_holdout.json)

secondary.beyond: vote 3 of 15; single coders 3 to 5 (s5-var 5); oracle 6
secondary.held_out_development: vote alone 62 of 94 (single coders 53 to 57, engine 65; against the engine 4 fixes and 7 breaks); engine-backed vote 63 against 67 for the same rule with s5-var's first program (it fixes none and breaks 2)

outcome.choice: engine-backed vote 63, not more than 69: no new method
outcome.reading: Agreement between separately trained coders is evidence where agreement inside one coder's beam was not (SeedLM-7: 52 -> 48): the condition of independence decides. On the real development tasks the vote beats every coder alone, but replacing the engine's unconfident programs with it loses: there the coders, all trained on the engine's programs and the same synthetic library data, share the engine's blind spots
